employeeInputs.source: Federal Form W-4 before 2020 or Nebraska Form W-4N
Federal Form W-4 before 2020 or Nebraska Form W-4N

steps: Subtract the payroll-period allowance value multiplied by allowances from Nebraska taxable wages.
Apply the appropriate filing-status and payroll-period percentage schedule.
Apply the special minimum-withholding procedure when the employer has more than 24 employees, unless adequate employee documentation supports a lower amount.
Add requested additional withholding and, for a qualifying nonresident, multiply withholding calculated on total wages by the Form 9N Nebraska allocation percentage.

specialMinimumWithholding.test: If ordinary withholding is less than 1.5% of taxable wages, increase it to at least 50% of the withholding for a single employee with one allowance or a married employee with two allowances.

missingStateCertificate.condition: Federal Form W-4 completed on or after January 1, 2020 without Form W-4N

supplementalWages.combined: Treat regular and supplemental wages as one payment.
separatelyPaidMethods: Aggregate with last preceding regular wages in the same year

residencyAndWorkRules.generalRule: Withhold for services performed in Nebraska; a multistate nonresident may provide Form 9N and withholding calculated on total wages is multiplied by its Nebraska percentage.

convenienceRule.appliesTo: Nonresident wages for work outside Nebraska for the employee's convenience that could have been performed for the Nebraska business in Nebraska
convenienceRule.sevenDaysOrLess: Both convenience wages and up to seven physical Nebraska workdays are exempt.
convenienceRule.moreThanSevenDays: Withhold only on wages for all physical Nebraska workdays; the threshold is retroactive to the first Nebraska day.

residencyAndWorkRules.militarySpouseElection: A qualifying nonresident servicemember spouse uses Form 9N for zero Nebraska allocation.

officialSpecialRuleExample.result: More than seven total Nebraska duty days; withhold on all 15 Nebraska days.

quarterlyReturn.due: Last day of month after quarter

monthlyDeposits.trigger: More than $500 withheld in the first month, or more than $500 in either the first or second month

filing.electronicPaymentTrigger: Total withholding payments in any prior year exceeded $5,000; mandate begins July 1 of the following year and continues.
filing.electronicInformationReturnTrigger: More than 50 wage and tax statements

captureWarnings: The special minimum rule is not simply max(ordinary tax, 1.5% of wages); the guide describes a 50%-of-reference-withholding alternative and allows documented lower withholding.
The seven-day convenience-rule transition is retroactive and therefore requires year-to-date day and wage state plus adjustment handling.
The complete wage-bracket matrices are retained in the checksummed official guide but are not transcribed.

review.requiredNextStep: Implement the documented-minimum exception and retroactive seven-day state, import wage tables, independently verify minimum-rule boundaries, and add formula, allocation, and transition regressions.
